details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> vulkan: fix out-of-bounds NVFP4 UE4M3 scale lookup (#31079) * vulkan : fix out-of-bounds NVFP4 UE4M3 scale lookup On the non-OCP path, ue4m3_fp32_lut has 128 entries and is indexed with the raw scale byte. ggml_validate_row_data accepts every byte and ggml_ue4m3_to_fp32 ignores bit 7, so a byte >= 0x80 reads past the shared array. Vulkan robustness does not cover shared memory. Size the table, both init loops, and the two host shared-memory budgets to 256 entries. ue4m3_to_fp32_build() already masks the exponent and treats only 0 and 0x7F as special, so entries 128-255 match the CPU. A 256-entry table keeps 0xFF distinct from 0x7F: the CPU decodes 0xFF as a non-zero value and 0x7F as zero. Each NVFP4 pipeline uses 512 more bytes of shared memory. ggml_fp32_to_ue4m3 never sets bit 7, so models quantized by llama.cpp are unaffected. Assisted-by: Claude Assisted-by: Codex * vulkan : fix out-of-bounds NVFP4 UE4M3 scale lookup Assisted-by: Codex --------- Co-authored-by: Dong

details.releaseNotesExcerpt: <details open> meta: support GLM-5.3 next sm tensor (#30499) * meta: support GLM-5.3 next sm tensor * glm5-next : cont q_absorbed for -sm tensor with non-unified KV * meta : keep GGML_OP_ARANGE in ggml.h order * glm5-next : split MLA heads in pairs for -sm tensor The MLA cache has a single KV head, so the heads on a device are its GQA ratio. The HIP tile FA kernel for D=512 needs an even GQA ratio; with 3 devices the 16 heads of the test model were split 5/5/6 and it aborted. * meta : keep the split for views inside one slab of the split axis With a non-unified KV cache, build_attn_mha splits q into streams with a view. For a permuted q, e.g. the absorbed query of glm5-next, that view aborted with "view of permuted tensor not implemented". The split is now kept if every other dim of the source and the view stays inside one slab of the split axis. The per-device strides are only rescaled above it. From tetherto/qvac-fabric-llm.cpp#353.
